## Online content

Since completing the MVA Master’s program, I have also followed
developments in technology and AI, mainly through
[Hacker News](https://news.ycombinator.com).

There are several high-quality online courses, books and articles freely available.
Among them, I particularly recommend:

**Mathematics and physics**

- Xavier Viennot’s course on
  [bijective combinatorics](https://www.viennot.org/abjc.html)
- Frederic P. Schuller’s course on the
  [mathematical foundations of theoretical physics](https://mathvideos.org/2015/frederic-schuller-lectures-on-geometrical-anatomy-of-theoretical-physics/)
- John Baez’s
  [*What Is Entropy?*](https://math.ucr.edu/home/baez/what_is_entropy/index.html)

**Machine learning**

- Aurélien Géron’s
  *[Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn and PyTorch](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/hands-on-machine-learning/9798341607972/)*
- Jeremy Howard and Sylvain Gugger’s
  *[Practical Deep Learning for Coders](https://course.fast.ai/)*
- François Fleuret’s
  *[The Little Book of Deep Learning](https://fleuret.org/public/lbdl.pdf)*
- A review of the history of
  [diffusion models](https://baincapitalventures.notion.site/Diffusion-Without-Tears-14e1469584c180deb0a9ed9aa6ff7a4c)

## Science outreach

In 2023, I participated in the project
[Regards de Géomètre](https://lesmathsenscene.fr/regards-de-geometre/),
organized by *Les Maths en Scène*.
The aim was to combine mathematics and artistic creation.

The slides from my presentation, intended for high school students
(in French), are available here:
[PDF](assets/pdf/rdg.pdf).

## Reading

A selection of books I have particularly enjoyed.
I would be happy to receive recommendations in a similar spirit.

- Albert Lautman: *La pensée mathématique et la réalité physique* (1952)
- Richard P. Feynman, Robert B. Leighton, Matthew Sands:  
  *The Feynman Lectures on Physics* (1964)
- Saunders Mac Lane: *Mathematics: Form and Function* (1986)
- Donella H. Meadows, Dennis L. Meadows, Jørgen Randers,  
  William W. Behrens: *The Limits to Growth* (1972)
  
## Miscellaneous

- Y.-J. Ringard: [Mustard Watches](https://girard.perso.math.cnrs.fr/mustard/article.html)
- [How I Read Your Tutorial (as a Beginner)](https://anniemueller.com/posts/how-i-a-non-developer-read-the-tutorial-you-a-developer-wrote-for-me-a-beginner)
- Bartosz Ciechanowski’s
  [*Lights and Shadows*](https://ciechanow.ski/lights-and-shadows/)

This website is built using [Quarto](https://quarto.org), an open-source, Markdown-based system for scientific and technical publishing.

See my [blog post](/posts/posts-1/) on setting up an academic website with Quarto and GitHub Pages.
